g.text: Web app, DB schema, repository layer
Written per course, NOT by us
The instructor owns the two yellow boxes.
It is an ordinary JUnit or pytest suite. We do
not generate it, invoke it, or constrain how
it is structured. It imports the reporting
library and calls us with the target names the
instructor registered in the web app.
The marking logic lives here too. Under the
AUTOGRADER policy, whether a target gets AI
feedback on failures only, on a subset, or on
a superset is a decision she expresses in this
run_autograder is hers as well: it decides to
run her suite and then invoke our AI phase.
Thin by design: two calls, an HTTPS client,
and argument validation. One artifact per
It rejects an unregistered target name loudly
on the first call, failing her test run. A
typo that silently succeeds is the worst
failure mode here: everything looks like it
worked and the feedback simply never appears.
Invoked by the instructor's autograder script
as a separate command after her suite exits,
not from inside her test code.
Resolves the marks, errors if a registered
target was never reported, grades the tasks
whose target is marked IMMEDIATE, leaves
NIGHTLY ones alone, and packages results.json.
Log in, then click Rerun Autograder once per
submission that still has tasks marked
ai_needed. It does NOT call an LLM and does
AD-5: the container holds the instructor's
own LLM API key** and calls the providers
directly. Our service never proxies an LLM
call and never sees a provider key.
For an OER this is the right default: each
adopting institution uses its own key and pays
its own bill, so nobody has to run a metered
service or handle someone else's billing.
The container still holds NO database
credential. It reaches our data only through
Two things to settle in the instructor guide,
not in code. How the key gets into the
container, which depends on what secret
facility the platform offers; if the only
route is the uploaded autograder zip, say so
plainly, because a key in a zip is a key in a
backup. And that rotation means touching every
